turnaround_reason: N-able, a SaaS provider of unified endpoint management, security, and data protection for MSPs, fell from ~$8.7 to ~$4 as a go-to-market transition and UEM/EDR renewal challenges forced a full-year guidance cut. It is basing near multi-year lows but the most recent catalyst (the guide-down) was negative.
bullish_points: High-quality SaaS economics: ~80% gross margins, ~$70M FCF, and a ~29-30% adjusted EBITDA margin target for 2026
Data Protection ARR crossed $200M and is growing faster than the company, leading net-new ARR — a genuine bright spot
Cheap for software: forward P/E ~9.4, price/book ~0.95; net revenue retention still positive at ~106% reported
Sticky MSP customer base; $50k+ ARR customers up ~7% YoY and now ~63% of ARR (up-market mix improving)
Balance sheet workable (current ratio 1.3, ~$116M cash) with product investment shifting to AI-driven security and DR
bearish_points: The most recent catalyst was a guidance CUT: FY26 ARR lowered to $562-565M from $581-586M on UEM/EDR renewal problems — momentum is the wrong way
ARR growth has decelerated to ~4-6%; this is a low-growth SaaS name, not a re-acceleration story yet
Go-to-market transition is mid-stream with execution risk and no proven inflection
EV/EBITDA ~16.3 is not cheap on cash earnings despite the low P/E; heavy share count (~189M) dilutes per-share metrics
No open-market insider buying (grants only); only 5 analysts and a 'none' consensus recommendation
catalyst: Stabilization of UEM/EDR renewals and continued Data Protection ARR growth; a guidance beat/raise would reset sentiment
suggested_trade: Pass / watchlist. Revisit only if Q3 shows renewals stabilizing and ARR guidance holds or ticks up
key_risk: Renewal churn in UEM/EDR continues and the GTM transition stalls, so ARR growth fades toward flat and the multiple compresses
would_skip_if: Another ARR guidance cut, net revenue retention drops below ~100%, or Data Protection growth decelerates
